title: Government Websites that Meet Standards for Access by Persons with Disabilities
what_it_is: Government Websites that Meet Standards for Access by Persons with Disabilities

sections.label: Government website accessibility standards
sections.summary: Government websites must meet WCAG 2.0; 90% of audited agency sites complied over three years, and FY2017 will add SS618 and Citizen Connect Centres.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Our Government websites are required to satisfy the WCAG 2.0 requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Over the past three years, 90% of the agencies' websites audited complied with the WCAG 2.0 requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Those which did not comply were required to improve their websites to the standards within several months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: During this financial year (FY) 2017, we will enhance the digital standards for our Government websites beyond WCAG 2.0, as we continue to raise their level of inclusivity and usability for more users.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: For example, we will incorporate the new Singapore Standard SS618 by the Standards, Productivity and Innovation Board (SPRING) Singapore, "Guidelines on User Interface Design for Older Adults", that aim to further enhance the online user experience of our websites, such as having audio captions in large font.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: For citizens, including PWDs who need further help to transact online, or who do not have Internet access, Citizen Connect Centres (CCCs) have been set up at various Community Centres/Clubs to assist them in this regard.

sections.label: Compliance assurance for government websites
sections.summary: Over three years 90% were compliant, non-compliant sites became compliant, and the speaker has reasonably high assurance almost all government websites comply.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Over the last three years, 90% were compliant and those that we detected that were not compliant, they became compliant.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: I have a reasonably high assurance that almost all our Government websites are compliant.
